text: Though you mount on high as the eagle, and though your nest is set among the stars, I will bring you down from there,” says Yahweh.
context: Obadiah says that even if Edom sets its nest among the stars, it will be brought down.

text: For this I will lament and wail; I will go stripped and naked; I will howl like the jackals, and moan like the daughters of owls.
context: Micah says he will wail like the jackals and mourn like the ostriches.

text: The chariots rage in the streets. They rush back and forth in the wide ways. Their appearance is like torches. They run like the lightnings.
context: Nahum pictures chariots racing like torches through Nineveh's streets.

text: Their horses also are swifter than leopards, and are more fierce than the evening wolves. Their horsemen press proudly on. Yes, their horsemen come from afar. They fly as an eagle that hurries to devour.
context: The Chaldeans' horses are described as swifter than leopards.

text: Herds will lie down in the middle of her, all the animals of the nations. Both the pelican and the porcupine will lodge in its capitals. Their calls will echo through the windows. Desolation will be in the thresholds, for he has laid bare the cedar beams.
context: Zephaniah says herds will lie down in Nineveh and the raven will lodge in the capitals.

text: In that day, says Yahweh of Armies, I will take you, Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel,’ says Yahweh, ‘and will make you as a signet, for I have chosen you,’ says Yahweh of Armies.”
context: Yahweh says he will make Zerubbabel like a signet ring.

text: Again I lifted up my eyes, and saw, and behold, four chariots came out from between two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
context: Zechariah sees four chariots coming out from between two bronze mountains.

text: When you offer the blind for sacrifice, isn’t that evil? And when you offer the lame and sick, isn’t that evil? Present it now to your governor! Will he be pleased with you? Or will he accept your person?” says Yahweh of Armies.
context: Malachi asks if a governor would accept a blind or lame animal as a gift.

text: Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed became the father of Jesse.
context: Matthew's genealogy names Salmon, Boaz, Ruth, and the line down to David.

text: James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);
context: Jesus gives James and John the name Boanerges, which means Sons of Thunder.

text: and Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others; who served them from their possessions.
context: Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, is among those who support Jesus.

text: Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
context: Simon Peter cuts off the right ear of Malchus, the high priest's servant.

text: They put forward two, Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus, and Matthias.
context: They put forward Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus, and Matthias.

text: Greet Rufus, the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
context: Paul greets Rufus, the chosen in the Lord, and his mother.

text: If any man doesn’t love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be cursed. Come, Lord!
context: Paul writes a warning and closes the line with Maranatha.

text: I exhort Euodia, and I exhort Syntyche, to think the same way in the Lord.
context: Paul urges Euodia and Syntyche to agree in the Lord.

text: Luke the beloved physician and Demas greet you.
context: Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas send greetings.

text: The greeting of me, Paul, with my own hand, which is the sign in every letter: this is how I write.
context: Paul says the greeting of his own hand is the sign in every letter.

text: Send Zenas, the lawyer, and Apollos on their journey speedily, that nothing may be lacking for them.
context: Paul asks that Zenas the lawyer and Apollos be sent on their way with care.

text: The children of your chosen sister greet you. Amen.
context: The letter ends with greetings from the children of your chosen sister.

text: I wrote to the assembly, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, doesn’t accept what we say.
context: John says he wrote to the church, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first, rejects them.

text: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like the Son of God), remains a priest continually.
context: Melchizedek is described as without father, mother, or genealogy.

text: But this you have, that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
context: The letter to Ephesus commends them for hating the works of the Nicolaitans.

text: that you shall say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers:’ that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.”
context: Joseph tells his brothers that every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.

text: Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
context: The census notes that Zelophehad had no sons, and names his daughters.

text: I thank God that I baptized none of you, except Crispus and Gaius,
context: Paul says he baptized only Crispus and Gaius, besides the household of Stephanas.

text: Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
context: The prophets and teachers at Antioch include Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, and Lucius.

text: but he was rebuked for his own disobedience. A mute donkey spoke with a man’s voice and stopped the madness of the prophet.
context: Peter recalls that a donkey speaking with a man's voice restrained the prophet's madness.

text: of the tribe of Judah twelve thousand were sealed, of the tribe of Reuben twelve thousand, of the tribe of Gad twelve thousand,
context: The sealed list begins with twelve thousand from the tribe of Judah.
